folds.text: Sometimes Claude gives an answer that sounds sure but is wrong. This is called a **hallucination**.
Typical culprits are made-up quotes, invented web links, wrong dates and books or studies that do not exist. Odd details are the riskiest.

items: Ask Claude where a fact comes from, then open that source yourself.
Compare with a trusted website or a second source.
Check names, numbers and quotes first.

folds.text: Treat Claude like a smart colleague, not a source of truth. The more it matters, the more you check: health, money, legal and school work.

folds.prompt: One part of this answer is made up. Tap it.

segments.text: Paris is the capital of France.
The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.
It was designed by Leonardo da Vinci.
It is made mostly of iron.

folds.why: The tower was built by Gustave Eiffel's company, not da Vinci. Claude can sound sure and still be wrong.
